sources.entry: Bdash - Modern SQL client application, supports MySQL, PostgreSQL (Redshift) and BigQuery.[![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon] ](https://github.com/bdash-app/bdash) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]
Bdash - Simple SQL Client for lightweight data analysis.

summary.one_liner: Bdash is a simple SQL client desktop app for lightweight data analysis, with query saving, charting, gist sharing, and an MCP server for AI coding tools.
summary.what_it_does: Bdash is a SQL client for running queries against several databases and reviewing the results. The README lists saving queries and drawing charts as features, and says results can be shared as a GitHub gist. It supports MySQL, PostgreSQL (including Amazon Redshift), SQLite3, Google BigQuery, Treasure Data, and Amazon Athena. It also includes an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that lets AI coding tools such as Claude Code list data sources, tables, and saved queries, read table schemas, and write or create queries in Bdash's editor. The README describes installation via the website or GitHub releases, and includes development and release instructions.
use_cases: Run SQL queries against MySQL or PostgreSQL databases
Query BigQuery, Athena, or Treasure Data from a desktop client
Save and reuse frequently used SQL queries
Chart query results for quick data analysis
Share query results as a GitHub gist
Let an AI coding assistant read schemas and write SQL in Bdash
notable: Built-in MCP server so Claude Code and similar AI tools can list schemas, read and write queries in the editor
Supports MySQL, PostgreSQL/Redshift, SQLite3, BigQuery, Treasure Data, and Amazon Athena
Query results can be drawn as charts and shared via GitHub gist
Bundled macOS app includes the MCP server at a fixed path inside the app
caveats: README does not describe platform support beyond a bundled macOS app path
MCP setup requires manually editing a Claude Code settings file with an absolute path
Feature sections for saving queries, charts, and sharing have little detail in the README
